sections.title: Key Debuts and Free Content
items: Mega Mewtwo X and Mega Mewtwo Y debut in Super Mega Raids. Mewtwo caught from these raids unlocks at least Mega Level 1 and can Mega Evolve into the defeated form without the initial Mega Energy cost; completing raids also awards Mega Energy.
The global event is free for all Trainers; log in to access habitats, bonuses, Special Research, and increased Shiny opportunities.
Zeraora makes its global debut through Special Research. Each Trainer can receive at most one Zeraora encounter; duplicate GO Fest Special Research awards Zeraora Candy instead.
Bulbasaur, Charmander, and Squirtle wearing Pikachu sun visors appear and can evolve for the first time; Pikachu wearing team-themed hats also appears.

sections.title: Saturday Habitats and Raids
items: 10:00–13:00 “Stormfire Peaks” (Ice/Electric/Fire): Mega Ampharos, Mega Blaziken, and Mega Abomasnow in Mega Raids; Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Lugia, and Ho-Oh in 5★ raids.

13:00–16:00 “Stellar Tides” (Psychic/Ghost/Water): Mega Alakazam, Mega Gengar, and Mega Swampert in Mega Raids; Uxie, Mesprit, Azelf, Dialga, Palkia, Altered Forme Giratina, Origin Forme Giratina, Xerneas, Yveltal, Solgaleo, and Lunala in 5★ raids.
16:00–19:00 “Dragonflight Peaks” (Flying/Rock/Dragon): Mega Pidgeot, Mega Aerodactyl, and Mega Salamence in Mega Raids; Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza, Reshiram, Zekrom, and Kyurem in 5★ raids.
Saturday Super Mega Raids: Mega Mewtwo X.

sections.title: Sunday Habitats and Raids
items: 10:00–13:00 “Forged Grounds” (Ground/Steel/Normal): Mega Metagross, Mega Garchomp, and Mega Audino in Mega Raids; the Regi trio, Origin Forme Dialga, Origin Forme Palkia, Heatran, Regigigas, both Formes of Tornadus/Thundurus/Landorus, both Formes of Enamorus, Regieleki, and Regidrago in 5★ raids.

13:00–16:00 “Verdant Anomaly” (Bug/Grass/Poison): Mega Beedrill, Mega Pinsir, and Mega Sceptile in Mega Raids; all four Formes of Deoxys, Genesect with multiple Drives, Nihilego, Buzzwole, Pheromosa, Xurkitree, Celesteela, Kartana, Guzzlord, Necrozma, Stakataka, Blacephalon, and the Tapu family in 5★ raids.

16:00–19:00 “Twilight Battlefield” (Dark/Fairy/Fighting): Mega Tyranitar, Mega Gardevoir, and Mega Lucario in Mega Raids; Latias, Latios, Cresselia, Darkrai, Cobalion, Terrakion, Virizion, Zacian (Hero of Many Battles), and Zamazenta (Hero of Many Battles) in 5★ raids.

sections.title: Official Community Celebrations
items: Official community celebrations are confirmed in multiple cities across North America, Europe, Oceania, and Asia-Pacific on 7/11 or 7/12, mostly from 10:00–19:00 local time; RSVP on the official page.

regions.calendar-notes:
Headline: Pokémon GO Fest 2026: Mega Finale

September 5 and September 6 use two different daily Mega Raid pools: Mega Mewtwo X headlines the first day, followed by Mega Mewtwo Y on the second. Remote Raids are unlimited, so plan your passes, healing items, and main attackers in advance.

8/17–22: This week’s windows

  • 8/17 Max Monday: Magikarp runs from 6:00–21:00, with a featured 18:00–19:00 window; complete an in-person Max Battle to receive one Rare Candy XL.
  • 8/18–24 Ultra Unlock: Water Festival increases Catch XP and Stardust in stages, with the highest multipliers near the end.
  • 8/22 Starmie Super Mega Raid Day offers boosted Shiny odds, 5,000 bonus XP per raid, and up to six free Raid Passes.

8/31–9/4: Mega Ascension daily pools

  • During Mega Ascension, Mega Latias and Mega Latios may appear throughout.
  • 8/31: Mega Victreebel, Mega Dragonite, and Mega Malamar; 9/1: Mega Falinks; 9/2: Mega Skarmory.
  • 9/3: Mega Starmie; 9/4: Mega Raichu X / Y. Each day has a different pool, so do not leave a target until the next day.

9/5–6: Two separate Finale pools

  • The 9/5 daily pool has 15 habitat Mega Raid Bosses, plus Mega Mewtwo X at select Gyms; Bug-, Psychic-, Ghost-/Dark-, and Electric-type Mega Evolutions are the day’s main targets.
  • The 9/6 daily pool changes to 16 different habitat Mega Raid Bosses, plus Mega Mewtwo Y; Steel-, Ice-, Water-, Flying-, Fairy-, and Dark-type targets are concentrated on the second day.
  • Both days rotate hourly from 10:00–18:00; prioritize targets by the date on which they appear.

Regional and in-person events

  • 9/12–13 Kuala Lumpur KLCC Park in-person event is the first stop of the PokéXciting Asia-Pacific tour, featuring teal-costumed Pikachu and local / cross-region stamp routes.
  • 9/23–27 Dancing in the Moonlight is limited to Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Indonesia, Singapore, Hong Kong, and Malaysia, with several daily Clefairy outbreak windows.
regions.rankings-current:
Today’s priority: clear the 8/17 limited windows, then stock up for Mega Finale

Dynamax Magikarp is available today from 6:00–21:00, with a featured 18:00–19:00 window; “Choose Your Path: Venom and Vines” ends at 20:00. If you still plan to raid Groudon or Mega Garchomp, finish before the route bonus ends.

Current raids: Ice teams offer the best return

  • Groudon remains through 8/18, and Water-, Ice-, and Grass-type teams all perform well. Mega Garchomp is double weak to Ice, so prioritize a strong Ice attacker lineup.
  • Shadow Giratina (Altered Forme) is available only on weekends. Prepare Dragon-, Ghost-, Dark-, Ice-, and Fairy-type teams in advance, but do not mistake it for an all-day target today.
  • Full teams and movesets are in “Current Raid Counters”; this priority panel does not repeat the whole table.

8/18–24: Resource week and Raid Day

  • Water Festival raises Catch XP from ×2 to ×4 and Stardust from ×3 to ×5. If your schedule is flexible, save high-volume catching for the later, higher-multiplier stages.
  • Starmie Super Mega Raid Day on 8/22 combines a boosted Shiny window, bonus Raid XP, and free passes. Prepare Electric-, Grass-, Bug-, Ghost-, or Dark-type attackers.
  • Dynamax Magikarp is easy, so prioritize Electric- or Grass-type Max damage and avoid overinvesting for a single rotation.

Featured: Prepare for Mega Finale

  • The daily Mega pools differ from 8/31–9/4. List the forms for which you lack Energy or have not unlocked; Mega Latias and Mega Latios span the lead-up event and can serve as flexible targets.
  • September 5 and September 6 use two different pools, headlined by Mega Mewtwo X and Y respectively. Allocate Raid Passes, healing items, and friend-group times by target date.
  • For team building, prioritize Ice, Ghost / Dark, Fighting, and Ground, then add Electric and Grass coverage for Water-type targets. These groups cover many bosses in both the current pool and the Finale.
